# 1 Samuel Chapter 29 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 167r | **Source Image:** 1SA_029_page_001.jpg

---

**29:1** And-gathered [the]-Philistines all their-camps to-Aphek, and-Israel [was]-encamping by-the-spring which [is]-in-Jezreel.

**29:2** And-[the]-lords of-[the]-Philistines [were]-passing-on by-hundreds and-by-thousands, and-David and-his-men [were]-passing-on in-the-rear with-Achish.

**29:3** And-said [the]-commanders of-[the]-Philistines, "What [are] these Hebrews?" And-said Achish to-[the]-commanders of-[the]-Philistines, "Is-not this David, servant of-Saul king of-Israel, who has-been with-me these days or-these years? And-I-have-not found in-him anything from-[the]-day of-his-falling [to me] until this day."

**29:4** And-were-angry with-him [the]-commanders of-[the]-Philistines. And-said to-him [the]-commanders of-[the]-Philistines, "Send-back the-man, and-let-him-return to his-place which you-appointed for-him there, and-let-him-not go-down with-us into-the-battle, and-let-him-not become for-us an-adversary [satan] in-the-battle. And-with-what could-this-one reconcile-himself to-his-lord? Is-it-not with-the-heads of-these men?

**29:5** Is-not this David of-whom they-sing in-the-dances, saying, 'Saul has-struck his-thousands, and-David his-ten-thousands'?"

**29:6** And-called Achish David and-said to-him, "[As]-YHWH lives, indeed you [are]-upright, and-good in-my-eyes [is]-your-going-out and-your-coming-in with-me in-the-camp, for I-have-not found in-you evil from-[the]-day of-your-coming to-me until this day. But-in-[the]-eyes of-the-lords you [are]-not good.

**29:7** And-now return and-go in-peace, and-you-will-not do evil in-[the]-eyes of-[the]-lords of-[the]-Philistines."

**29:8** And-said David to-Achish, "But what have-I-done, and-what have-you-found in-your-servant from-[the]-day I-was before-you until this day, that I-may-not go and-fight against-[the]-enemies of-my-lord the-king?"

**29:9** And-answered Achish and-said to-David, "I-know that you [are]-good in-my-eyes, like-an-angel of-God. But [the]-commanders of-[the]-Philistines have-said, 'He-shall-not go-up with-us into-the-battle.'

**29:10** And-now rise-early in-the-morning, and-[the]-servants of-your-lord who came with-you — and-rise-early in-the-morning, and-when-there-is-light for-you, go."

**29:11** And-rose-early David, he and-his-men, to-go in-the-morning, to-return to-[the]-land of-[the]-Philistines. And-[the]-Philistines went-up to-Jezreel.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **29:4 — satan** (שָׂטָן): "Adversary" — the common noun meaning "opponent/accuser," not yet the proper name of a supernatural figure. The Philistine commanders fear David will become their *satan* in battle.

2. **29:6 — Achish swears by YHWH**: A Philistine king swearing by Israel's God — perhaps diplomatic courtesy, or reflecting genuine recognition of David's deity.

3. **29:8 — David's ambiguous reply**: "The enemies of my lord the king" — deliberately ambiguous. David leaves unclear whether "my lord" means Achish or Saul, and who "the enemies" are.

— EMET
